Header: Eleusine indica Uganda: kasibanti; Myanmar: myet-thakwa, se-gwa, sin-ngo-let-kya; Vietnam: co' cu'a ga, co man trau, co ong

Prevention: Purchase certified crop seed and animal feed to reduce the chance of contamination
As seeds can travel on animals and machinery, do not allow animals into an affected area, limit machinery use in the area and keep machinery clean to prevent spread
Keep crop healthy to maximize competitiveness - use optimal water and fertilizer levels
For pasture, encourage good grass coverage since grass can outcompete the weed.
Limit the amount of grazing in a particular area:
Supply multiple watering points to prevent livestock congregating
Monitoring: Tufted annual grass, spreading or stands straight, up to 60 cm tall
Seedlings: first leaf is about 1 cm long, pointed, may lie flat on soil
Leaves: bright green; smooth; flat to
V-shaped; up to 8 mm wide, 15 cm long.
Tends to form a long-growing rosette with white-coloured leaf sheath at the base
Does not root at nodes of growing stems.
Seeds: reddish-brown to black; oblong; ridged; about 1 mm long
Roots: centralized system; very strong when mature
Spreads along disturbed habitats such as roads and powerline corridors.
Look for it along marshes, stream banks and coasts
Can be confused with weeds such as
E. indica is distinguished by the combination of its flattened stem, bright green leaves, size and many- flowered character of spikelets, lack of awns.
Direct Control: Remove by hand if the weed is smaller than 5-8 cm in diameter.
Use a hoe if removal is difficult.
Removal gets harder as weed grows (root system is stronger)
The weed grows best in compact, poorly drained soils so make sure it is aerated and drained
Use solarization to kill weed seeds down to 5 cm.
This requires watering (light irrigation) of the soil area after mulching and before covering the area with the transparent polyethylene sheet
Use shredded newspaper as a mulch on tomato fields
Use a rye cover crop – its residues should supress the weed
